_comment: 30 golden queries: 15 en, 10 id, 5 mixed (code-switching). expected_doc_ids reference eval_doc_id in corpus.json. Cross-lingual queries (id question -> en doc) intentionally test multilingual embedding quality.

queries.question: What mechanism does the Transformer architecture rely on instead of recurrence and convolutions?
expected_answer_points: relies entirely on attention mechanisms
self-attention relates all positions in parallel
multi-head attention
positional encodings inject order information

queries.question: How is BERT pre-trained and what objectives does it use?
expected_answer_points: masked language modeling predicts hidden tokens from both directions
next sentence prediction
pre-trained on unlabeled text then fine-tuned

queries.question: What are the main limitations of retrieval-augmented generation?
expected_answer_points: answer quality is bounded by what the retriever surfaces
hallucination can persist when retrieved evidence is only partially relevant

queries.question: How does DPR compare to BM25 for open-domain question answering?
expected_answer_points: dense dual-encoder outperforms BM25 by a large margin
top-20 retrieval accuracy
trained with in-batch negatives

queries.question: What is in-context learning and how does model scale affect it?
expected_answer_points: tasks specified through text without gradient updates
few-shot demonstrations in the prompt
scaling model size smoothly improves in-context learning

queries.question: How does LoRA reduce the cost of fine-tuning large language models?
expected_answer_points: freezes pre-trained weights
trains low-rank decomposition matrices
up to ten thousand times fewer trainable parameters
no additional inference latency after merging

queries.question: What is double quantization in QLoRA?
expected_answer_points: quantizes the quantization constants themselves to save memory
combined with 4-bit NormalFloat
backpropagates through frozen 4-bit base model into adapters

queries.question: How can dense retrieval work in a zero-shot setting without any relevance labels?
expected_answer_points: language model generates a hypothetical document answering the query
the hypothetical document is embedded and used for nearest-neighbour search
encoder bottleneck filters hallucinated details

queries.question: What is late interaction in ColBERT and why is it efficient?
expected_answer_points: queries and documents encoded independently as token embeddings
maximum-similarity operator computed afterwards
document representations precomputed offline
two orders of magnitude faster than cross-encoders

queries.question: Why is standard BERT impractical for large-scale sentence similarity search, and what is the alternative?
expected_answer_points: BERT requires feeding both sentences jointly
SBERT uses siamese networks to produce fixed-size embeddings
cosine similarity comparison reduces search from hours to seconds

queries.question: Can Transformers be applied directly to images without convolutions?

needs very large pre-training data to beat convolutional networks
matches or exceeds state-of-the-art with less training compute

queries.question: Which parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods allow adapting very large models on limited GPU memory?
expected_answer_points: LoRA trains low-rank adapters on frozen weights
QLoRA fine-tunes through a frozen 4-bit quantized model
65B model on a single 48 GB GPU

queries.question: What approaches exist for making neural retrieval faster or cheaper than full cross-encoder ranking?
expected_answer_points: late interaction with precomputed document embeddings
siamese sentence embeddings compared by cosine similarity

queries.question: How do retrieval-based systems keep generated answers grounded and updatable?

queries.question: What did GPT-3 reveal about the relationship between model size and task performance without fine-tuning?

smooth improvement with scale
